newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee council now set to meet May 7.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee council now set to meet May 7.

text.p: Brazil's new coffee council, known as the CDPC, is now to hold its second meeting on May 7 as opposed to an earlier date of May 5, said the vice-president of the growers' National Coffee Council.
No reason was given for the delay, said Manoel Bertone, who is also a council member.
The council unites six private sector and six government representatives under its president, Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles.
Council members will hold a preparatory meeting on May 6 in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais state, Bertone said.
One of the key issues to be discussed at the council will be a report by think-tank Fundacao Getulio Vargas (FGV) on ways to resolve producer debts.
The report is due to be sent to the Industry and Commerce Ministry at the beginning of next week, Bertone said.
Producers are hoping that the FGV proposals will be officially approved at the May 7 meeting.
Also likely to be on the agenda is Brazil's position ahead of a May 21 council session of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).
ACPC member countries are to discuss at the London council whether to continue market stabilisation mechanisms in 1997/98 (July/June).
